summary.text: An addition reaction is an organic reaction in which two or more molecules combine to form a larger molecule called the adduct.
It is limited to compounds with multiple bonds, such as an alkene with a carbon–carbon double bond or an alkyne with a triple bond.
It is the reverse of an elimination reaction, in which one molecule divides into two or more molecules.

facts.label: Product
facts.value: The larger molecule formed is called the adduct

facts.label: Starting molecules
facts.value: Compounds with multiple bonds, such as alkenes and alkynes

facts.label: Reverse reaction
facts.value: Elimination; dehydration reverses an alkene's hydration to alcohol

items.prompt: Two small molecules join to make one larger molecule in an addition reaction. What is that larger molecule called?
items.explain: In an addition reaction, two or more molecules combine to form a larger molecule called the adduct.

items.prompt: A chemist needs a starting material for an addition reaction. Which molecule is ruled out?

options.label: An alkene with a carbon–carbon double bond
An alkyne with a carbon–carbon triple bond
A molecule with a carbonyl group (C=O)
A straight chain with only single bonds and no rings

items.explain: Addition is limited to compounds with multiple bonds, and rings also count as points of unsaturation, so a plain chain of single bonds is out.

items.prompt: Water is added across an alkene to make an alcohol. A chemist then removes the water again by dehydration. What general kind of reaction is that reverse step?
items.explain: An addition reaction is the reverse of an elimination reaction, and the hydration of an alkene is reversed by dehydration.

items.prompt: Which pair names the two main types of polar addition?
items.explain: Electrophilic and nucleophilic addition are the polar types, while free-radical addition and cycloadditions are non-polar.

items.prompt: A product made by addition then reacts further and ejects a leaving group. What is this two-part sequence called?
items.explain: Depending on the product structure, it could react further to eject a leaving group, giving the addition–elimination sequence.

items.prompt: A molecule has a carbon double-bonded to oxygen, a carbonyl group. Can it take part in an addition reaction?

options.label: No, only carbon–carbon multiple bonds can
No, only molecules with rings can
Yes, because carbon–heteroatom double bonds can undergo addition
Yes, but only after turning into an alkene

items.explain: Molecules with carbon–heteroatom double bonds, such as C=O or C=N, can undergo addition reactions.
